name: bada-sokudoku
description: Bada Sokudoku — a speed-reading studio that solves the page as an image, and watches the reader with the same encoder. A Swin-style windowed self-attention encoder with shifted windows runs over the patch grid of a scanned or photographed book page; attention rollout inside each window partition, fused with classic run-length smearing, recovers the character clusters, lines, blocks and the reading order (right-to-left for vertical Japanese). The recovered blocks are then lit one after another at a dwell time derived from the reader's perceptual span and target speed, and the same windowed-attention encoder is turned on the reader through the camera (skin-chroma, darkness and motion patch features; largest component is the face, the valley in its upper band gives the eyes, pupil and head offsets give a gaze index) so that fixations, saccades, regressions, blinks and the follow rate are counted live. Page and reader are composited into a single canvas so the whole thing can be recorded to WebM as it runs; no frame ever leaves the device. No OCR, no network, self-contained HTML.
author: Masaaki Yamaguchi
